questions.q: Why can't a standard role-hierarchy sharing rule cleanly handle access for high-volume external (Customer Community) users?
options: High-volume external licenses typically sit in a flat, non-hierarchical structure, so role/group-based rules don't map cleanly onto them
Sharing rules only work on standard objects, never custom objects
External users can never be granted record access under any circumstances
Sharing rules require Modify All Data, which external users can never hold
questions.explain: High-volume external user licenses are designed to avoid giving each portal user an individual role for performance and administrative reasons, so hierarchy-based sharing tools don't apply the way they do internally — which is exactly the gap Sharing Sets fill.

questions.q: What does a Sharing Set's access mapping actually define?
options: A static field-value condition identical to a criteria-based sharing rule
A role hierarchy specifically for portal users
A rule connecting a lookup field on the record (e.g., Account) to the logged-in external user's own Account or Contact
The Apex RowCause used for programmatic sharing to external users
questions.explain: The access mapping grants access based on a relationship evaluated per user and per record — typically 'this record's Account equals my own Account' — rather than a static criterion.

questions.q: An admin builds a technically correct Sharing Set access mapping on the Case object, but a Customer Community User still sees zero cases. What is the most likely cause?
options: The org-wide default for Case must be changed to Public Read/Write first
Sharing Sets cannot be applied to the Case object under any configuration
The admin needs a second Sharing Set layered on top of the first
The Customer Community User profile itself was never given object-level Read access to Case
questions.explain: A Sharing Set only adds access on top of what the profile already permits — if the profile itself lacks object-level access, the access mapping has nothing to grant on top of.

questions.q: For a role-structured partner population (e.g., Partner Community users organized by role), which mechanism replaces the Sharing Set?
options: Manual sharing performed by each partner user
Share Groups, which can target public groups, roles, or roles-and-subordinates instead of profiles
Organization-wide defaults set to Public Read Only
Apex Sharing Reasons defined on the User object
questions.explain: Share Groups are the role-based equivalent used for partner/role-structured external licenses; profile is not a valid member type there, unlike in a Sharing Set.

questions.q: An external user's access depends on a calculated eligibility flag that no lookup-based access mapping can express. What should the architect reach for?
options: Converting all affected external users to internal licenses
Raising the object's org-wide default to Public Read/Write
A second, nested Sharing Set referencing the first
Apex managed sharing, inserting rows on the record's share object under a custom reason, the same mechanism used internally
questions.explain: When the declarative Sharing Set access-mapping language can't express the needed logic, Apex managed sharing is the fallback — it works identically for external and internal users.
